title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #16

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An orphan is (1 mark)
   A. a person who looks after children
   B. a woman whose husband has died
   C. a brother or a sister
   D. a child whose parents have both died

2. The mother of your husband or wife is your (1 mark)
   A. care-giver
   B. ancestor
   C. mother-in-law
   D. sister-in-law

3. Which article do we use before 'honest man'? (1 mark)
   A. an
   B. a
   C. the
   D. some

4. What is a surname? (1 mark)
   A. Your family name
   B. Your first name
   C. Your address
   D. Your school

5. Which word has both the sounds /ɔɪ/ and /l/? (1 mark)
   A. oil
   B. boy
   C. toy
   D. road

6. Which word stays the same in the plural? (1 mark)
   A. cow
   B. sheep
   C. hen
   D. goat

7. An open-ended composition (1 mark)
   A. has no words
   B. must copy a story
   C. has only one correct answer
   D. gives you a topic and you decide the story

8. Which is the best first step before answering a question on a passage? (1 mark)
   A. Read the question and find key words
   B. Write the answer immediately
   C. Close the book
   D. Copy the passage

9. Which of these words is written with a double consonant in the middle? (1 mark)
   A. dinner
   B. drink
   C. play
   D. stop

10. Which word contains the blend 'tr'? (1 mark)
   A. snake
   B. flag
   C. clap
   D. train

11. What does 'bleed' mean? (1 mark)
   A. To sleep
   B. To sing
   C. To eat too much
   D. To lose blood from a cut

12. A friendly letter is written to (1 mark)
   A. a stranger only
   B. the government only
   C. someone you know well
   D. nobody

13. Which sentence would be best in the body of a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. Yours faithfully
   B. To whom it may concern
   C. I hope you are well.
   D. Sincerely, the Manager

14. Why is it important to plan a composition? (1 mark)
   A. It keeps the ideas in order
   B. It hides your ideas
   C. It stops you from writing
   D. It makes the story longer without ideas

15. Which word helps to show order in a narrative? (1 mark)
   A. suddenly
   B. eleven
   C. blue
   D. table

16. Which question ends with a rising voice? (1 mark)
   A. Did you save the file?
   B. When did you save the file?
   C. How did you save it?
   D. Who saved the file?

17. A dialogue is (1 mark)
   A. a picture only
   B. a list of nouns
   C. a poem with no words
   D. a conversation between two or more people

18. 'Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.' Sugar is (1 mark)
   A. a plural noun
   B. uncountable
   C. countable
   D. a verb

19. What is the negative form of 'We are shouting'? (1 mark)
   A. We not are shouting.
   B. We do not shouting.
   C. We are not shouting.
   D. We are no shouting.

20. Which sentence shows two actions going on at the same time in the past? (1 mark)
   A. I cooked and my sister washes plates.
   B. I was cooking while my sister was washing plates.
   C. I have cooked while she washed.
   D. I am cooking and my sister was washing plates.

21. Which word needs a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. week
   B. Friday
   C. morning
   D. season

22. Which pair of words differs only because of /v/ and /w/? (1 mark)
   A. vet and wet
   B. sip and chip
   C. bell and bill
   D. sit and sat

23. Why is fast reading not always good reading? (1 mark)
   A. Fast readers cannot use their eyes
   B. Books are meant to be read slowly only
   C. Speed is never important
   D. Mistakes and lost meaning mean you must read again

24. Which word helps to show the order of events? (1 mark)
   A. heavy
   B. suddenly
   C. farm
   D. green

25. Which of these can spread HIV? (1 mark)
   A. Hugging a friend
   B. Playing football together
   C. Sharing a razor blade
   D. Sharing a plate of food

26. What does an adverb tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How many things there are
   B. More about a verb, such as how, when or where
   C. The name of a place
   D. A person's name

27. Why do flies spread germs? (1 mark)
   A. They drink clean water
   B. They land on waste and then on food
   C. They eat all the soap
   D. They sleep on beds

28. Which conjunction gives a choice? (1 mark)
   A. or
   B. so
   C. and
   D. yet

29. Which sentence uses 'nor' correctly? (1 mark)
   A. She has no soap, nor water has she.
   B. She has no soap, nor does she have water.
   C. She has no soap, nor she does have water.
   D. She has no soap nor does have water she.

30. Which word begins with the unvoiced sound /θ/? (1 mark)
   A. they
   B. that
   C. thank
   D. the

31. Which word has the consonant cluster /sk/? (1 mark)
   A. goal
   B. desk
   C. ball
   D. race

32. Why should you not click on strange pop-up advertisements? (1 mark)
   A. They are required by the teacher
   B. They may be unsafe
   C. They are always free prizes
   D. They improve your reading

33. Which is the best answer to 'When does the match begin?' (1 mark)
   A. On the field.
   B. It is mine.
   C. At ten o'clock.
   D. The referee.

34. Which is a factual question about the passage? (1 mark)
   A. What job did Class Six do?
   B. Why do you think the head teacher smiled?
   C. What kind of person is Kamau?
   D. Was the clean-up a success?

35. When I arrived, the bus had left. Which happened first? (1 mark)
   A. I arrived.
   B. Both together.
   C. The bus left.
   D. Neither happened.

36. What is the past participle of 'eat'? (1 mark)
   A. eaten
   B. eating
   C. eated
   D. ate

37. Which preposition completes: 'The clock is ____ the door.' (higher than, not touching)? (1 mark)
   A. under
   B. behind
   C. above
   D. below

38. What comes after a preposition in a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. A question mark
   B. A noun or pronoun
   C. A full stop
   D. Another preposition

39. Which word ends with a double consonant? (1 mark)
   A. clas
   B. cla
   C. clasp
   D. class

40. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'glad'? (1 mark)
   A. happpy
   B. hapie
   C. hapy
   D. happy

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. What kind of person is Kamau in 'The Clean-Up Day'? Give a reason from the text. (3 marks)

42. Explain why we say 'a university' but 'an umbrella'. (3 marks)

43. Write two minimal pairs for /l/ and /r/. (2 marks)

44. Give two pieces of advice for staying safe online. (3 marks)

45. Give three safety rules for using the internet. (4 marks)

46. Explain two ways to make a story interesting. (4 marks)

47. Give two nonverbal cues that show a speaker is confident. (2 marks)

48. List the five parts of a friendly letter. (3 marks)

49. Punctuate: 'mama may i go to the shop' (2 marks)

50. Write four sentences about cleaning your classroom that use and, but, so and or. (4 marks)

51. Explain how a word wheel can help you make new words. Give an example with the ending -oy. (4 marks)

52. Explain why 'She asked where the clinic was?' is wrong and correct it. (3 marks)

53. State the difference between a factual question and an inferential question. (2 marks)

54. In the passage 'The Purse in the Market', what did the purse contain? (2 marks)

55. List three things a child must never give to a stranger online. (3 marks)

56. Write four sentences to advise classmates on keeping the school toilets clean. (4 marks)

57. Give the meaning of four words from the lesson: injury, treatment, painkiller, poison. (4 marks)

58. Write four words with double consonants and four words with blends. (4 marks)

59. Give two reasons why we plan before writing a story. (2 marks)

60. Write two similes about food. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — a child whose parents have both died
   An orphan has lost both parents.

2. C — mother-in-law
   The mother of your husband or wife is your mother-in-law.

3. A — an
   The h in honest is silent, so an is used.

4. A — Your family name
   The surname is the family name.

5. A — oil
   Oil has /ɔɪ/ followed by /l/.

6. B — sheep
   Sheep is both singular and plural.

7. D — gives you a topic and you decide the story
   You use your own ideas to complete it.

8. A — Read the question and find key words
   Key words tell you what to look for in the text.

9. A — dinner
   Dinner has double n.

10. D — train
   Train begins with t and r.

11. D — To lose blood from a cut
   A bleeding wound loses blood.

12. C — someone you know well
   A friendly letter is personal.

13. C — I hope you are well.
   It is a warm, friendly opening line.

14. A — It keeps the ideas in order
   A plan shows what comes first, next and last.

15. A — suddenly
   Time words show order.

16. A — Did you save the file?
   It is a yes or no question.

17. D — a conversation between two or more people
   It shows what people say to each other.

18. B — uncountable
   We cannot count sugar one by one.

19. C — We are not shouting.
   Not comes after are.

20. B — I was cooking while my sister was washing plates.
   'While' links two past progressive actions.

21. B — Friday
   Days of the week begin with capital letters.

22. A — vet and wet
   In 'vet' and 'wet' only the first sound differs.

23. D — Mistakes and lost meaning mean you must read again
   Rushing causes errors that hurt understanding.

24. B — suddenly
   'Suddenly' is a time word.

25. C — Sharing a razor blade
   HIV can pass through blood, so razor blades must never be shared.

26. B — More about a verb, such as how, when or where
   Adverbs answer how, when and where.

27. B — They land on waste and then on food
   Flies carry germs from waste to food.

28. A — or
   'Or' offers choices.

29. B — She has no soap, nor does she have water.
   After 'nor', the helping verb comes before the subject.

30. C — thank
   'Thank' has the unvoiced 'th'.

31. B — desk
   'Desk' ends in sk.

32. B — They may be unsafe
   Strange links can be unsafe.

33. C — At ten o'clock.
   'When' asks for a time.

34. A — What job did Class Six do?
   The answer is stated in the text.

35. C — The bus left.
   The past perfect shows the earlier action.

36. A — eaten
   Eat, ate, eaten.

37. C — above
   'Above' means higher than.

38. B — A noun or pronoun
   For example: 'on the table'.

39. D — class
   Class ends in ss.

40. D — happy
   Happy has a double p.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Observant and responsible: he noticed a hole in the fence and said it should be fixed at once.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality and 1 for evidence.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Both start with the letter u, but university starts with the consonant sound 'yoo', so it takes a. Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so it takes an. We choose by sound, not by letter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example and 1 mark for the sound rule.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: light, right and load, road.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not give your name, school or address to strangers. Show worrying messages to a trusted adult. Ask a parent or teacher before opening a new page.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct piece of advice, up to 3.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use it with an adult, keep your password secret, do not give your name or address to strangers, tell an adult if something frightens you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule, up to 4.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Start with something that makes the reader curious, and add small details or similes. These help the reader picture the story and want to continue.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each way explained.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Eye contact and standing straight; a smile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Address, date, greeting, body, closing and name (address and date may be given together).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for address and date, 1 mark for greeting and body, 1 mark for closing and name.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mama, may I go to the shop?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for capitals and comma, 1 for the question mark.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four correct sentences, each with the named conjunction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: A word wheel has a fixed ending and different beginning letters. You change the first letter to make a new word. With -oy you can make boy, toy and joy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fixed ending, 1 mark for changing the first letter, 1 mark each for two correct words.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: It reports a question, so it is a statement and needs a full stop. Correct: She asked where the clinic was.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reason, 1 for correction, 1 for full stop.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: A factual question has an answer stated in the text. An inferential question needs you to use clues and think.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each type.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: It had some coins and a card with the name Mrs Achieng Odhiambo.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the coins and 1 mark for the card.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name, home address, school name, password.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each, up to 3.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands with soap after using the toilet. Do not throw rubbish in the latrine. Keep the door closed. Tell the teacher about any damage.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible sentence.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Injury: harm done to the body. Treatment: care given to a sick person. Painkiller: medicine that reduces pain. Poison: something that can make you very ill or kill you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Double: letter, dinner, apple, bottle. Blends: train, snake, clap, flag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct group of two words, up to 4.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: It puts ideas in order and makes sure we do not forget important events.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: The bread was as soft as a pillow. The juice was as sweet as honey.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
